ORAL JUDGMENT :
1. Heard.
2. ADMIT.
Taken up for final disposal with the consent of learned counsel for the parties.
3. Despite the attempt was made, non applicant No.2 could not be served.
Report which is on record shows that non- applicant No.2 has already performed marriage and staying alongwith her husband.

3. Present application is preferred by the applicants who are husband and relatives of the husband for quashing of the FIR in connection with crime No.272/2012 registered with Police Station Ambazari District Nagpur for the offences punishable under Section 498-A read with Section 34 of the IPC and consequent proceeding arising out of the same bearing charge- sheet No.136/2012 having RCC No.889/2013.
4.
The crime is registered on the basis of the report lodged by non-applicant No.2 on an allegation that her marriage with applicant No.1 was performed on 05.06.2009.

After 12 apl 1113.19.odt..odt marriage she resumed cohabitation at the house of the applicants but she was not treated well and she was ill treated on the ground that she is not good looking and her sister in law dislike her and applicant No.1 has committed a mistake by performing marriage with non-applicant No.2.
She suspected character of her husband.
On the basis of the said report police have registered crime against the present applicants.
5. Heard learned counsel for the applicants who submitted that on the basis of omnibus general allegations applicants are implicated in the alleged offence.

He further invited my attention towards the documents which show that out of compromise the applicant No.1 and non-applicant No.2 has preferred the petition for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent.
The consent terms were recorded.
In view of the consent terms non-applicant No.2 agreed to withdraw the allegations which are made by her in the FIR and also agreed to consent for the quashing of the FIR.
In view of the above said settlement the decree of dissolution of marriage is passed on 20.01.2015 and thereafter this petition came to be filed for quashing of the FIR.

In 12 apl 1113.19.odt..odt view of the settlement terms between the applicants and non- applicant No.2.
6. Perused the recitals of the FIR wherein it appears that general and vague allegations are levelled as far as applicants are concerned.
On the basis of omnibus, vague and general allegations the applicants are implicated in the alleged offence.

As far as the allegation regarding the illicit relations between the applicant No.1 and his sister in law is concerned, it is also vague allegation without specifying any specific instances on the basis of which she has suspected the character of the applicant No.1.
Regarding allegation of demand is also appears to be vague.
7. Now considering that applicants have approached to this Court for quashing of FIR as the settlement terms are settled between them.
In view of the said settlement terms, the applicant No.1 Rajiv S/O Dinanath Mate And 2 Others vs State Of Mah., Thr. Pso P S Ambazari P S ...

2 has already paid an amount of Rs.6 Lakhs to the non- applicant No.2 towards full and final settlement and she agreed to quash the FIR and thereafter the present application came to be filed.

The report of the police also from the statement of the friend of non-applicant No.2 it revealed that she has performed 12 apl 1113.19.odt..odt the marriage and now she is residing alongwith her subsequent husband.
The general diary entry is also taken to that effect.

Considering the settlement terms which are recorded before the Competent Court, in view of that decree of dissolution of marriage is also performed, he submitted that prima facie case is not made out against the present applicants.
In view of that the application deserves to be allowed.

8. Per contra, learned APP strongly opposed the said contentions and submitted that there is a prima-facie material against the present applicants hence, the application deserves to be rejected.
6.
On going through the entire investigation papers and specially settlement terms, it reveals that out of settlement, decree of dissolution of marriage is already passed.

The settlement terms are also placed before the competent Family Court and in view of that Family Court has passed decree of dissolution of marriage.
12 apl 1113.19.odt..odt 9.

In view of above facts and circumstances application deserves to be allowed.
10.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following order:-
ORDER (i) The Criminal Application is allowed.

(ii) The FIR in crime No.272/2012 registered with Police Station Ambazari, District Nagpur for the offences punishable under Section 498-A read with 34 of the IPC and consequent proceeding arising out of the same bearing charge-sheet No.136/2012 having RCC No.889/2013 is quashed and set aside to the extent of applicant Nos. 1 to 3 namely Rajiv s/o Dinanath Mate, Yash s/o Dinanath Mate and Sadhna w/o Yash Mate.
11.
The criminal application stands disposed of in the above said terms.
Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
